questions.q: Which four kinds of information does MLflow record for a run?
options: Parameters, metrics, artifacts and models
Datastores, environments, compute and endpoints
Tables, views, indexes and schemas
Commits, branches, tags and pull requests
questions.explain: MLflow tracks parameters (settings), metrics (numeric results), artifacts (files) and models (packaged model folders) for each run.

questions.q: Inside a training job running on an Azure ML compute cluster, what do you need to do before calling mlflow.log_metric?
options: Call set_tracking_uri with the workspace URI and sign in through a browser
Nothing extra: the tracking URI is configured automatically and a run is started for you
Install the Azure ML SDK v2 logging module
Register the metric name in the studio first
questions.explain: Microsoft's docs say the tracking URI is configured automatically in jobs on compute clusters, notebooks and compute instances, and in a job you can log without calling start_run. SDK v2 has no logging module of its own.

questions.q: mlflow.autolog() reported training_accuracy_score of 0.854 while held-out test accuracy was about 0.75. What is the right conclusion?
options: Autolog is broken and should never be used
The model improved during evaluation
The two numbers must always be equal
Autolog logged scores on the training data, so you should still log test-set metrics yourself
questions.explain: The metric names begin with training_, so they are computed on training data, which usually looks better than test data. Autolog is convenient but you must choose the metric you trust.

questions.q: In Azure ML, why do you sort the DataFrame from mlflow.search_runs with pandas sort_values rather than the order_by argument when ranking by a metric?
options: Pandas is faster than MLflow
order_by only works on runs from the last day
Azure ML does not currently support order_by expressions containing metrics.*, params.* or tags.*
search_runs never returns metrics
questions.explain: Microsoft's query guide notes that order_by does not currently support metrics, params or tags expressions, so you sort the returned DataFrame with pandas instead.

questions.q: When would you need to call mlflow.set_tracking_uri with your workspace's URI?
options: Every time you submit a command job
When your code runs outside Azure ML, such as on your laptop, and you want its runs tracked in the workspace
Only when using the studio Metrics tab
Only for AutoML jobs
questions.explain: Azure-hosted compute is configured automatically. Code running elsewhere needs mlflow, the azureml-mlflow plugin, and the workspace tracking URI (read from the workspace via ml_client).
